diarization.text: Yes. He's usually my voice of reason, but I tend to just keep taking on more to see what I'm capable of. I think he's right that I'm pushing myself toward a breaking point.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is that how you see it too? What extra things do you take on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: At my last job, I took on extra roles to get experience in assessments and case management. Even now, I took on an extra group at work. I'm hourly, so I'm actually working for free preparing for it at home. It's an anger management group, and I'm learning while I teach it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Working for free sounds difficult. Why do you do it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I was raised to work hard and keep building my resume. I find it hard to say no. I often regret it once I'm in the middle of it, but I hold so much value in gaining experience and learning more.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What are the most important things to you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Work and school. I struggle because I don't place relationships at the highest point, which some people look down on. My friendships make me happy, but the work environment I'm in now is draining. It's high-stress and full of crises, unlike my last job with adults with disabilities.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Your previous job sounded more collaborative and supportive.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It was. I dread going to work now because of the structural problems and the negative environment, but I feel like I have to stay for the experience. I don't have time to apply for other jobs right now, so I feel stuck.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've thought about quitting, but I hate disappointing people and letting the team down. However, the team isn't really invested in me, and the atmosphere is very negative. Several other new case managers have already quit.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I miss my old job. I only left because I moved back here. They wanted to promote me, but they knew I was moving, so they only gave me a temporary position to get some experience.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It sounds like that was the right environment for you, and you don't have that now. Do you feel your concerns are being heard at your current company?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They hear me, but they don't know how to fix the negative attitude of the long-term staff. They even ask me for advice on how to fix the team because of my past supervisor experience. It's a lot of pressure.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I have a constant need to please people, so it's hard to be honest about the flaws I see. It's draining to come into that environment every day. I feel exhausted by the time I get home.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I wonder if I should find a new job, but applying is just more stress. Last week, I had a client pass away and another was attacked by her boyfriend. After doing everything I could to help her, she just went back to him. I felt completely helpless.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're feeling that guilt that even though you did everything, it wasn't enough.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Exactly. I want a mindless job while I'm in school, like being a receptionist, but then I feel like I'd be wasting my time and not getting experience. I need the challenge to feel like I'm worth something, but I also need the validation that I'm working hard.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm proud of myself when I challenge myself. I question my worth if I'm not doing a lot. My dad instilled that work ethic in me, but he doesn't think school is worth the money, so I feel I have to work extra hard to prove that I'm still being productive.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: We're wrapping up for today. Is there anything else on your mind?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just trying to figure out how to balance everything. I wish I had an extra day in the week, but I just have to keep powering through.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: We can pick up on that struggle next week. It was nice meeting you, Tanya.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Okay. Thank you.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #38 - Symptoms of Hoarding Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of hoarding disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm doing all right. How about you?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm doing well, thanks for asking. I understand you've had some recent difficulties and that brought you into our agency.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'm having some problems with friends and family, relationships I guess in general. I have a lot of stuff.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You have a lot of stuff?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, a lot of stuff. My house is full of things and it's kind of embarrassing. I don't like to get rid of things. I worry that I'm going to need them or something. So, yeah, it's overflowing my house with stuff.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So there's a lot of stuff in your house. And this is affecting your relationships?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, there's all this stuff is taking over my house. There's no room for anyone to really come over and visit me, which is really become a problem. You meet people, it's normal to go over to their house and have lunch or whatever, and I get really embarrassed. I don't want people to do that. I don't want my family even coming over. My sister was over last week and she threw something away. She threw this newspaper away from two years ago and I freaked out. What if I need that? You know, those things are important to me. So that's kind of putting a strain on my relationship with my family in that way. I think they're the only ones probably that would feel brave enough to actually do something like my sister did.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: She threw something away?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, so yeah, it's just embarrassing that I can't have my friends over. I'd like to have my family over and I just can't. I don't know what to do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you mentioned your house is overflowing. How cluttered? Can you describe it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: There's room for me to live in there. But there's a path from my front door to the kitchen and to my bedroom and the bathroom. But sometimes it's blocked by stuff when things fall or whatever. But pretty much my whole house, I'd say, is full of things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And what type of things? You mentioned a newspaper.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I don't like to get rid of cards or newspapers or magazines, mail, things like that. But I've also collected things over the years. I inherited the house from my grandmother, so all her stuff was in there and I really can't get rid of that. That all has a lot of sentimental value to me. So my things have just kind of been piled up on her things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So you have a lot of stuff in the house and it's congested, but you're able to move around and live there.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'm not freely able to move around, but it works for me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: But it would be difficult or it is difficult when other people come by.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, they wouldn't really be able to be in there.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Now, some of these items you said you received when you received the house. Do you ever go out and buy things and bring them in?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I like to go shopping. I like to go to yard sales on the weekends. I'm kind of a deal hunter. So if I see a good deal, I don't want to pass it up. If it's a good deal, I might not be able to come back to it. So I do like to buy things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How often do you buy things?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Probably on the weekends I go to yard sales. I usually buy a few things every weekend from the yard sales, they're such a good deal. So I make a trip to the mall or TJ Maxx or something once a week at least. So I usually buy something then too.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Does your vehicle have stuff in it now that you bought?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, I actually picked something up that I saw that was for sale on the side of the road on the way here. It was a little bedside table, so it was only a few bucks, so I bought it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So you have some things you buy, you have some things that you otherwise obtain that are in the house and they're already there. And you have trouble parting with them.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever tried to throw anything out or give anything away?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: People have suggested that I do that, but I just can't bring myself to do that. I mean, like my sister came over, she tried to get rid of something for me, and I just couldn't do it. You know, it's too hard. I just think I might need it, you know? What if I need it? What if I want to look back and reference that newspaper that she tried to throw away? I won't have it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So what would you like to gain from counseling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I would like to be able to get rid of things. I would like not to worry so much when I do or when someone wants me to. So I can kind of gain relationships with people. People don't really want to come over. I mean, they don't like to come over. I don't like them to come over and it kind of puts a strain on relationships, especially my dating relationships. I don't want to tell people about it. I don't want people to see that, that's embarrassing to me. So significant others kind of think that's weird and that kind of think I'm shady because I don't want them to come over, like I have something to hide or something. But I mean I do, but they don't know that's what it is.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you'd like to be able to throw things out and clear out your home.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, a little bit at a time. I don't think it's going to happen right away, but I'd hope to get there eventually. Just start working on it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. I have a couple other questions. Do you have any medical problems?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any history of mental health disorders, drug or alcohol use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, I mean, I drink socially with friends.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Socially? Nothing else?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, that's it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you're doing okay at work?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I love my job. I work as a call receiver at a call center, so yeah, I get along with everyone. My boss thinks I do a great job, so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay, great. All right, Jackie, if you're okay with it, I'll get you in to see a counselor. We'll get that scheduled.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I look forward to that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay, great. Thanks.

video_details.title: Simulation Scenario - Adolescent Risk Assessement
video_details.description:
This video demonstrates an adolescent psychiatric risk assessment, focussing on risk of suicide and self harm and assessment of mental state. This could be used prior to simulation training as a stand-alone or part of a course to demonstrate best practice. 

For more clinical simulation resources please visit http://ww2.clinsim.health.wa.gov.au/

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Heidi, my name's Dr. Sarah, one of the emergency doctors. I'd like to chat with you about what's been going on and how you've been feeling, so we can find out how best to help you. Would that be alright?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Everything we talk about will be confidential unless I think that you're at risk of being seriously harmed or someone else is. In that case, I'd need to tell someone so we could make sure everyone is safe. Is that okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It seems like your mom's pretty worried about you. But I'm curious, are you worried or concerned about anything at the moment?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, everything's fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. How's your mood been recently?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Crap.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Crap. Like, how?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just crap. I don't care about anything, don't want to do anything.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So how have you been spending your time filling up your days?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just lying in bed all day doing nothing, just thinking. I've got these thoughts.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah. Go on.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: These thoughts of dying.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You think about dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: All the time. Just every day.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you think about how that could happen?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think I'll probably jump off a bridge.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Which one?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: There's a really high bridge near my house called the Swing Bridge.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Why that one?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's really high so I know I'll die if I jump off, but there's also a train track underneath. So if the fall doesn't kill me, then the train will.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you made any plans about actually going there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just thinking all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And what's stopped you from going there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: My mom. She'd probably be really upset if I did it, but things have just gotten worse and I can't take it anymore.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you think about how you could get to the bridge?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've been looking at bus timetables today for the bus that goes by the bridge. I think I'm going to do it tonight. I just can't take it anymore; she can't treat me this way.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever done anything else to hurt yourself?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Like what?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Sometimes when people are struggling like you are, they can do other things to hurt themselves like burning or cutting.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I cut up my legs.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: When was that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Today, yesterday, every day.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever done anything else to hurt yourself?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, just cutting.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Heidi, do you ever have thoughts about harming anyone else?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I'd never harm anyone else.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever see or hear things that other people can't?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I don't think so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Who are you living with at the moment?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just Mom and Jack, my younger brother.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How are things at home?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not good. Mom's always having a go at me and today we had a massive fight. It's just getting worse and she can't treat me this way.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And Jack?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Jack's three, so he gets what he wants.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have someone you can talk to about these thoughts about wanting to die?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I talk to Sophie. She's my friend. She wants to die too, so I know she won't tell anyone.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Heidi, I know some young people have experiences with drugs and alcohol. Do you drink alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, sometimes, just with my mates.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you had anything alcoholic to drink today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What about other drugs, like pot or ecstasy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is there anything else you want to let me know?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any questions for me?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thank you for talking to me today. I'm worried about you being at risk of hurting yourself, so I'd like my colleague John, a mental health nurse, to have a chat with you. Would that be okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It'll be about half an hour. Can I get you something to drink while you wait?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, can I have a Coke?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Sure.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi, is that John? This is Sarah from ED. I've just conducted a risk assessment on a 14-year-old, Heidi, with a history of depression and self-harm. Her mum's worried she'll try and end her life tonight. Heidi has ongoing thoughts about jumping off a bridge and has been looking at bus timetables. I'm worried she might act impulsively. She regularly cuts her legs. She's currently calm and cooperative. Can you come and assess her to see if she needs admission?

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #39 - Symptoms of Illness Anxiety Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of illness anxiety disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I guess okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. I understand you've had some recent difficulties that have brought you in here today.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, well, my physician, I've been seeing her, meeting with her, and she suggested I come see you, so yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Why do you think she did that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, well, I'm sick, I think. So we've been running some tests and things and she couldn't find anything. So she thought maybe I should come talk to you, I guess maybe my concerns are, I don't know, coming from somewhere else, I think is what she thinks. But, I don't know, maybe whatever illness I have is making me feel this way.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you believe you have a physical illness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I just know there's something not right.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And your physician has run a series of tests?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, we've done like bloodwork and all the scans and everything, and she said she didn't find anything, but I just know there's something, there's something there.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So what was her, other than coming to see me, what was her suggestion for treatment, so she ran tests, she didn't find anything...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well yeah, she didn't, she didn't have anything for me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So she's saying there's no physical illness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's what she says. No, I think she's missing something.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How long have you believed that you've had a physical illness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: About a year, I think, is when my first appointment with my physician was. Yeah, when she started running some tests and things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so about a year ago you went to her, she started running tests, and there was no findings of a disorder?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, she hasn't found anything yet.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Was it just one disorder that you thought you had or have there been several?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: You know, I kind of started with MS. I read some things about that and how people my age have had it and they don't even know that they have it. And then, I guess after some tests and things, I just, I think it's cancer, that's what I'm worried about. Even though I don't really have some of the symptoms, it can just lie in you and you have no idea and it just one day, you know...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And your physician's run tests for all these disorders you think you have?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, but I mean, what if that test that I took a year ago didn't show up on that because it hasn't gotten that severe yet and now it is, so I'm worried.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you saw the physician for the first time regarding this a year ago. Did you have anxiety or worry before that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I just got that feeling that I was sick, so that was just what I was worried about, but nothing other than that, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, but you were worried about the illness. Nothing else though.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any physical symptoms?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, but that happens to people, you know, they don't experience any symptoms, they have no idea, and then it just, you're dead, you know.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find yourself checking often to see if you have physical symptoms or...?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah, I've read a lot of stuff, a lot of different people's stories. Go on the internet, check the symptoms and kind of keep track of that, make sure I'm not having anything that they list, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you active on the internet forums where they discuss illnesses and...?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah, I've read a lot of people's stories on there. I'm just, I'm worried I'm gonna miss something, you know, so I check a lot and check to make sure...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you read the forums. Do you ever post?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah, about my concerns, and sometimes people get a little frustrated with me, they're not very nice.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Tell me about that.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just because I'm not really experiencing anything, they think that I don't have anything to worry about and they keep telling me, but I think I do have something to worry about. I just have this feeling that there's something wrong, I just know it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What would you like us to do here at the agency?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I would just like to feel comfortable that I'm not sick. You know, I don't want to worry anymore, but I just really think I am, that there's something wrong. So...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah, you're worried you have a physical health disorder. Are you worried you have a mental health disorder?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Maybe, some people have said that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you worried about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's a little concern that I might be feeling a little extra worried, maybe that's a symptom of the, whatever illness I have, this one.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're concerned that the worry could be a symptom of a physical illness. So again, what would your goal be here? What do you want to change through counseling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess my worry, it doesn't make me feel good.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You want to worry less?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah. Yeah. I don't want to be sick. I don't want to be, I don't want it to be mentally ill either.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So you've had worry for at least a year. Specifically about being physically ill. There've been no findings of physical illness but you're still worried about it. And you might be a little worried that you have a mental health disorder.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I think something might be off, you know, something might be going on.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you want to be able to stop worrying about the physical health disorders. All right. Are you worried right now that you have a physical health disorder?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What disorder do you think you might have now?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Cancer, I think, just some part of my body, just worried that it's spreading.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you've been tested for this by your physician.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, but you know, sometimes tests don't find things. So...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you ever reassured when you get negative test results back, when they say there's nothing going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I just think they might've missed something. And my doctor, my family physician, she's just really frustrated with me because she won't even see me anymore, honestly. She's not very nice when I go in. But I want her to do those tests again.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You want her to rerun tests and look again. All right. So you're open to counseling here?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah, I think maybe you can help me a little bit and find out what's wrong and what's going on. So...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Would you be okay signing a release so I could talk to your physician?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah, that's fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So I'll get you scheduled now. I'll get you into to see a counselor, it'll just take a couple days and we'll get that worked out now.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Okay, great. Thank you.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thanks.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #40 - Symptoms of REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of REM sleep behavior disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm okay. How about you?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm doing well, thanks for asking. I understand you've been having some difficulties recently that have brought you into the agency.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'm recently married and my husband and I moved in together. Up until then I've lived by myself my whole adult life. So, apparently the craziest things have been happening while I've been sleeping. Several nights I've woken him up screaming very vulgar profanity words, and so that's a little alarming to him. I've even been hitting him in the middle of the night; he's waking up with these huge bruises on his arms. So yeah, apparently my behavior in the middle of the night is a little out of hand.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So I can understand why that would be distressing. Have you seen a physician about this?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, I participated in a sleep study and...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What'd they say?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They've ruled out some other things and thought that maybe it was a behavior sleep disorder, so they have referred me to you. I'm still working with them while they run some tests, but they thought maybe there were some other stressors or underlying things that might be going on.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So what would you like from counseling? Like, what would a goal be?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, I'm just a little worried that it's going to affect my marriage and that my husband will not be able to deal with it. So I would just really like to figure out how to keep my relationship with him successful and overcome these issues.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So after your yelling things or you hit him while you're asleep, when you wake up, what's going through your mind then?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Usually I wake up and he's like, 'What are you doing?' and I say I was having the worst dream. Those dreams are kind of aligning with what my behavior is. I don't feel anything myself. I have fallen out of bed a couple times and woken up, but I didn't really think anything of it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: But now you're starting to wonder.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it's a little strange and a little concerning.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're starting to wonder if you didn't have this disorder before.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I wouldn't have known because I lived by myself. But I had fallen out of bed a couple times and my sheets and pillows are always everywhere when I wake up, so I'm kind of making the connections now.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Does the episode of yelling or moving around happen any certain time, like right after you go to sleep or a while after?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: In the middle of the night. He said at first he thought I was joking around, but yeah, in the middle of the night I'm just waking him up.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Does it ever happen when you take a short nap?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, never happened then that I know of. He's usually around when I'm napping on the couch and he says it hasn't happened then.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So only at night when you're sleeping overnight and in the middle of that sleep. Would you be okay with signing a release so I can communicate with your physician?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Of course. Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And do you want your husband to be part of the counseling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that would probably be helpful for him to come in. He can give his side of things too.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you'd be okay signing a release for him?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, of course.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So I'll get you scheduled in to see a counselor. I appreciate you telling me what's going on; it's been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you. Thanks for your help.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #37 - Symptoms of Cannabis Use Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of cannabis use disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Good, I'm great.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're great?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I am.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm doing okay. Thanks for asking. I see that you signed a release so I could talk to your mother, and I see she took you in here today.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, she brought me in.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me what's going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Ah, she's she's not happy with me. She doesn't like that I smoke.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: She doesn't like how you smoke?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. I don't know why she's mad at me. But who cares, you know?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're concerned somewhat, but...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean I love my mom, you know, but I just kind of came here to make her happy, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And what are you smoking that has her concerned?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just weed. It's no big deal, really. I don't know why she's so upset.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: She's upset about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, she's been on me for a while about it, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are there any other drugs or alcohol or anything that you consume?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, yeah, I drink sometimes too. But not like...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Not something she's concerned with?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, I mean, no. She's more concerned about the weed, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you concerned with the alcohol or marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, no. I don't think it's a problem.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can I ask you a few questions about it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah. Sure. Of course.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me when you first started using it and how that came about?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think it was sophomore year of high school. One of my friends offered it to me, so I was kind of feeling having some anxiety, even had some anxiety about starting it, but so I tried it and it made me feel great. So it made my anxiety go away, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It took the anxiety away. How long did you have the anxiety before the marijuana use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Probably through my adolescence, a couple years. It wasn't anything crazy, but it affected my life a little bit, so I think it makes me feel a lot better now that I smoke it. It gets rid of that feeling.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you started marijuana because a friend offered it to you and because you were anxious. And then how about from then on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't want to feel that anxiety anymore. I don't want to have to take any pills or anything, so I've kind of just kept doing it to make me feel great. I think it's great.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. When was the last time you used?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: This morning.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Did anything happen in particular that you think motivated your mother to bring you in today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. I think she kind of wants me to get out and get a job and everything, but I'm living my life. It's perfectly fine, really. I've got a little bit of money, so I'm not worried.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So what do you want to happen? What would your goal be?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I want to make my mom happy, but I don't really want to stop.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: In order to make her happy, would you have to stop?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess. But maybe she could learn to deal with it if I just acted a little differently when I was on it. I don't really want to stop because it makes me feel so much better, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: She wants you to get a job, too?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, ideally she would like me to.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Would employment involve drug screening?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Probably some of them if I tried. I haven't really made a big effort to look for anything.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You don't have to worry about that right now.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I mean, every day is a new day, new chance for greatness and it's going great so far, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you mind if I ask you a few questions about your marijuana use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's perfectly fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever tried to cut down?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever taken in larger amounts than you wanted to or for longer periods?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean sometimes I'll smoke more than I usually do if I'm hanging out or maybe one of those anxiety days are a little worse, we'll smoke some more to...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How much time do you spend obtaining, using, or recovering from marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: A good amount of time. I love it, so it's something I love to do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's a big part of your life?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it's like my best friend.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have a craving for marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'd say so, I want to do it, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has it led to any social problems for you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I used to hang out with my friends a little more than I do, but I guess some of them think I do it a little too much.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do they?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has the marijuana use caused you to give up activities that were important to you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It is my important activity, you know? So, not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has the marijuana use caused any activity to become dangerous?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Like what?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Like driving while under the influence or anything like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I've done that. Is that dangerous? It's no big deal.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: That's dangerous.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm fine, you know? I usually drive. Everybody does that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Everybody does that? Now your mother, she drove you in today. Was she worried that you were under the influence of marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Probably, but she's kind of used to it, I guess. Not used to it, but she's aware of it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any history of mental health disorders?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just some anxiety, but other than that, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about medical problems?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, healthy as a horse.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you notice that when you stop using, you have physical symptoms or anxiety?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, yeah, I get the anxiety when I stop.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What's the longest you have stopped for?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Five minutes. I'm just kidding. Yeah, I smoke every day, so a couple hours while I sleep, a couple hours throughout the day, you know.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So it's an every day activity for you. And it's been that way for a while?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, past couple years, I would say.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right Jackie, I know that your mom wants you to get counseling here. Are you open to it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't really think I need it, but I'm sure once I leave here she's going to say I need to come back, so we'll see I guess.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're okay with giving it a try?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, we'll see.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. I'll get you scheduled to see a counselor and we'll see where that goes after your first appointment. Is that all right?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. I want to thank you for telling me what's going on and for answering my questions. It's been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you doc.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #35 - Symptoms of Schizoaffective Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actor) who exhibits symptoms of schizoaffective disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jason, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm okay. I'm alright.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're alright?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just here.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Just here?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just here.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I understand that you were in the hospital a couple weeks ago.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I was in the hospital about two weeks ago. I did something and I had to go to the hospital afterwards.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, so about two weeks ago I was finishing up this wonderful machine that I was creating in my room so that the government can't hear my thoughts or my actions or my behaviors. I was just trying to finish up my last little bit that I needed to build and I went over to the neighbor's because their garage was open. I just picked out a tool and I brought it back to the house. When I was in the house working on my room, the cops came and picked me up and took me to the hospital and I said, 'See, the government's at it again.'

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What do you think the government was trying to do?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They're trying to stop me from actually creating my room because they're creating this new order where they want everybody to follow them and I'm not a follower. I know what I want and I know what I need and I know what my family wants and I know what they need and I'm just trying to protect them by creating my room.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And tell me about your room. What are you doing there that makes that special?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: So I'm smart enough to know that there are frequencies and waves that are out there that the government is actually sending through the lights and also through the TV and like through every electronic apparatus that's out there. I've actually created a wave neutralizer so that it can actually stop that from happening so that you can actually live the life that you want and be happy and youthful and joyful all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is that how you were feeling when you were building it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, because I created this prototype in my room and anytime I'm basically in there, it was good. I had energy. I did all the calculations that I needed to create so I could actually build my system. Then I also did the calculations about the different types of waves being in the house but then also out of the house. Then I also had the opportunity to just not sleep because who needs sleep? I wasn't tired. And if I did sleep, I slept for like 15 minutes just because I needed to finish what I was going to do. And I was so close to finishing and my neighbor called the cops.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you had a period of time where you had like a lot of energy and you weren't really sleeping much?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, those two weeks. Doesn't everybody do that?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You were also happy and felt satisfied?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I felt good. Like, when I sleep, I don't like when I sleep because it just feels wrong. I'm not actually using my time wisely. So those last two weeks, or two weeks ago, it was perfect. It was the best time of my life. I was living life to my fullest then. It was perfect.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And how do you feel now in comparison?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm alright. I'm just alright right now. The government made me get on different medication. So I'm just alright. Not that happy, not that excited.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So not happy. How about sad?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I'm not sad either. It's just kind of in the middle. Just in the middle.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you want to get back to that happiness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Of course, who doesn't want to get back to the happiness of their life? That's the reason why I need to finish my machine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: The machine? Yeah. Now, you mentioned you'd ordered some products online. How much did you order?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think I ordered... the exact number: I ordered 236 hard drives. Because 236 is the perfect number that I needed to not only cover my bedroom so I could always be happy, but then within that 236 it also covered my house so that my family could be happy and like my four neighbors around us so we could all be happy. And that's the reason why I'm kind of angry at my one neighbor because I was including his house in on my grid so that he can also be happy all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: He would have been affected by your machine.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Of course. He's the one who helped me out, he let me borrow his tools, but evidently he didn't let me borrow them this time. So I'm going to just pull him out and I'll have another neighbor take his place.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Were all those hard drives fairly expensive?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't know. When I was up cleaning and running around the house trying to find more equipment, I found my mom's purse and I was just like, 'Oh my god, she has a credit card in there. Oh my god, I can use her credit card.' So I was using her credit card because I was trying to make her happy. And so I don't know, those 236, they were probably 50 to 100 dollars a piece depending on where I could get them and I just ordered them.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How'd your mother respond to that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, my mom came to the hospital and was just like, 'Where are all these boxes coming from?' I'm just like, 'Just put them in my room, mom.' She put them in my room and then like a week ago she was just like, 'I see you used my credit card,' and she wasn't too happy with me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is that a strained relationship?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, that's just how me and my mom's relationship generally is.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You get along okay with her?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: We get along perfectly fine. That's how we talk to each other. We talk to each other minimally because she's not in my room, so she's not happy. So anytime she does come into my room it messes up the balance, so I get unhappy and then I just tell her to stay out so that I can be happy and she can be happy in her own place.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you mentioned that they changed your medications in the hospital.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: The government changed my medication.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: The government? How are you feeling about taking your medications?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, the only reason I'm taking my medications now is because if I don't take them, then they're going to change them again and then that's going to delay me in finishing my wave generator. And I need to finish my wave generator. So I'm taking them because I don't want the government to have more power over me like they want to have power over everybody else.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I see you really want to get back to working on that machine.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, I want to be back in my happy place.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you found yourself as motivated these last couple weeks as you were before you were hospitalized?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I haven't been that motivated. I know I'm going to get it done. It's just I don't know if I'm going to get it done today or tomorrow, but I know it's going to get done.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You still want to get that done. It's important to you.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, it's really important to me because I can't be controlled by the government anymore.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, Jason. I'd like you to continue seeing a counselor here. Have you found the counseling to be helpful?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: The counseling has been okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's been okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I appreciate that they haven't been taking notes because I don't want that information to be leaked out. But it's been okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, well continue with counseling and I hope that that can help you a bit. I appreciate you spending this time with me and explaining what happened.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #36 - Symptoms of Cannabis Use Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of cannabis use disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, you know, I'm, I'm alright. How about you?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're alright? Yeah. I, I'm doing well, thanks for asking. I understand you've had some recent difficulties that brought you into our agency.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, yeah, I lost, I lost my job.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You lost your job?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh-huh. Um, because I failed a drug test. I have to drive a golf cart sometimes for my job and I just wasn't really paying attention as I was driving through the parking lot and I, I hit a car. Um, and I didn't think it was a big deal. It didn't even leave a big mark really, but the owner of the car got pretty pissed about it and they found out that I did it. I kind of admitted to it too. I didn't want to be getting in trouble for it. So then they, since it was an accident, you know, I kind of hit my head a little bit too. They made me take a drug test and, uh, I had smoked some weed the night before, so I failed it and was fired.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Were you aware that if there was an accident, you'd be drug tested?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, you know, I, I didn't know that, no. I guess they might have told me at some point but I, I probably wasn't paying attention to it or I wasn't prepared for it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hm. So there, has there been consequences to losing your job?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, yeah, I mean, my parents are not happy. Um, I'm not making any money, obviously, so they, uh, they're not very happy about me relying on them for, you know, gas money if I ever want to go anywhere or do anything with my friends. I have to ask them for money. So they're kind of, you know, pushing me to get a job and help support myself again.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, what type of work do you do?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I work in security. Um, I kind of, I monitor parking lot, you know, take tickets, things like that, so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So, most of those employers would require a drug screen?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's, that's my problem. Uh, I've been trying to look for a new job and, um, pretty much all of them have required drug tests, so I haven't gotten a new one yet. So that's becoming a problem. So that's why, you know, I want, I want to cut down but I haven't been able to. Um, so I really need a job. I mean, all these things are kind of silly that, you know, I don't, I find it silly. It should be, who cares if I smoke a little weed, you know, it should be legal.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You think it should be legal?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. I mean, what's the harm really? I didn't hurt anyone. So, so yeah, but I, I really do need a job. So I'm, I'm here to kind of get a handle on that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you want to stop using marijuana altogether?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'm going to have to to get a job I think, you know, I don't want to fail a random drug test again.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, can you tell me about your marijuana use now? Like, when was the last time you used?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, uh, I actually was hanging out with some friends or my roommate this morning. Well, not my roommate, but my friend that comes over and stays with me sometimes and we got high this morning, so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so recently. And how about the course? Like, when did you start using marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: A long time ago. I've been using probably since I mean, since I was in high school I started and it's kind of just been a big part of my life. I mean, my friends do it, all my friends do. Um, so, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Any other drugs or alcohol or anything? Just marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, just, just marijuana, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you noticed over time you've been using more?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean, you know, I try to cut down a little bit. I'll kind of say, 'Oh, just smoke a little bit,' and then, you know, when I'm hanging it with - hanging out with my friends, we'll end up just being high for a really long time and that's just what we'll do all night. So.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So it's consuming a lot of time, marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. Yeah, you know, I'm kind of always thinking about how I'm going to get more and trying to get a hold of my guy and so it really does take up a lot of my time and it's kind of a distraction. So.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. You have a craving for marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, no, I guess not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Now, have you had any social problems because of your marijuana use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I would say not other than my work. I mean, my friends all do it, they don't have a problem with it, so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are there other important activities that you miss out on because of your marijuana use? Outside of work.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Hmm, no, not - I mean, I don't really do a whole lot, so I don't really miss out on much.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You don't miss much. Are there any activities that you engage in that are more dangerous because of your marijuana use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Nah, we just kind of hang out in my basement and don't really do anything, so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any history of mental health issues or medical issues?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that. No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you notice any anxiety or physical symptoms when you stop using marijuana?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I feel - I feel okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Feel okay? Yeah. So how motivated are you to stop using?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't know, part of me doesn't really want to but it's something I have to do. You know, I need a new job. I don't want to be, you know, relying on my parents forever. It's pretty annoying. So, I'm pretty committed to it, I would say, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're committed to it? Yeah. I'm going to get you in to see a counselor here, if that's okay with you.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that would be really helpful.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It'll be helpful? Mm-hmm. And I appreciate you taking this time to tell me what's going on and answer my questions. This has been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #32 - Symptoms of Alcohol Use Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of alcohol use disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Jackie, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, how are you?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm okay, thanks for asking. I see that you have signed a release so I could talk to your mother and that she brought you in today. What's what's going on there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, you know they think I have a drinking problem, my family. So what really started this was this past weekend. They came to pick me up for my cousin's bridal shower and I was drunk when they came to get me so I couldn't go and now everybody's pretty pissed at me, so here I am.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So they asked you to come in to the agency?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, you know I don't want them to all hate me or anything so I agreed to come.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you believe that you have a drinking problem?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean I like to drink. I think it's okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You think it's okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I like it. I like drinking.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, you mind if I ask you a few questions related to your drinking?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, that's fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So how often do you drink now?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Pretty much everyday, I would think. Definitely everyday on the weekends for sure. During the week I'll go to whatever the best local happy hour is, so I'll go after work and have some drinks.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about on the weekend?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: On the weekend I kind of keep to myself, so I'll drink a little of whatever I have at the house. I don't really go out a lot on the weekend, mostly just stay at home and drink whatever I have there.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And how much are you drinking, let's say on the weekend?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's hard to keep track I think. I'd say maybe like two or three cases of beer throughout the weekend and then if there's something on sale at the liquor store down the street, I'll get like a bottle of vodka or something to go along with it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, and how about during the week?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: During the week I stay at the bar for a few hours, maybe have like six or seven drinks and then go home. I might have a glass of wine when I get home.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you drinking more than you want to?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess so. I've kind of tried to make a plan to just drink on the weekends and that hasn't really kept up because I like to go to the happy hours and stuff.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you've tried to cut down before and it hasn't worked for you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it's not really happening though. I don't really see it happening.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have cravings for alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: You could say so, yeah. When I'm at work I want to drink and when I'm out doing stuff I kind of want to drink.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you using exclusively alcohol or are there other drugs involved?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Right now just alcohol because it's legal. I was inpatient a couple times for cocaine but I've stopped that. It's not really something I want to do anymore.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: When was the last time you were inpatient?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: About four months ago, five months ago.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And at that time you used cocaine?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah I was using coke and drinking.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And why did you stop using cocaine?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well I graduated from college and then I had to get a job. I had a fear of losing my job because of the cocaine and I had to get a drug test and stuff, so that's kind of in the back of my mind. I think the treatment helped with that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you crave cocaine?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, mostly just alcohol.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about your work? Are you having any trouble keeping your job or has your performance been okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think I'm not doing the tip-top of what I could be doing, but it hasn't really been a problem. I haven't been threatened to be fired or anything, but I'll come in late every once in a while but I sneak in so nobody knows.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Any social problems because of the alcohol use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: With my family kind of right now, yeah, I'm not really getting along with them very well. My friends though, we get along fine but they're just not really as fun as they used to be.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Your friends?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, sometimes they want to do stuff like go to the movies and they get all mad because I don't want to go. I'd rather go party somewhere.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're having some social problems, not so much with your friends, a little bit, but more with your family?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: More with my family. I mean I guess my friends aren't that happy with me but I don't think it's a huge deal. My best friend and I haven't talked in a couple days because she was mad at me for not coming to dinner the other night because I'd rather drink and she didn't want to do that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So there have been some problems with the friends?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I guess so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you found that you're engaging in any activities that are physically dangerous because of alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've gotten hurt a couple times, I mean falling down the steps. I did sprain my ankle a couple months ago because I fell down the steps, but other than that I've been okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find that you have any exacerbation of symptoms that you have already? Like any medical or mental health problems made worse by the alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I'd say I'm pretty healthy.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Did you notice a point after you started drinking when you had to increase the amount that you drank to get the same effect?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And when did that happen?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think I kind of go through phases with it. I'll drink a certain amount for a while and then I'll notice yeah, I'm not even drunk anymore, so I'll have to drink some more.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: When was the last time you noticed that? When you noticed you had to drink a lot more to get the same effect?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'd say like last weekend. I was drinking a couple beers at my house and a few hours had passed and I had drank probably like 10, 12 beers and I wasn't feeling anything so I started drinking them a little faster and then I started feeling a little better.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about withdrawal? Do you have any symptoms of withdrawal when you stop drinking? Like physical symptoms, anxiety?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean I want some more for sure.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Cravings?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, crave some more, but I have a headache now, so...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right Jackie, are you open to seeing a counselor here at the agency?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think that's what my mom really wants, so maybe I'll try it out once or twice and see what happens, but I guess to make her happy I will.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, you'll try it out. I'll get you scheduled to see a counselor. I want to thank you for telling me about what's going on and for answering my questions. It's been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, sure.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #33 - Symptoms of Brief Psychotic Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actor) who exhibits symptoms of brief psychotic disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hey Jason, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I'm okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just okay. Just, um, some things that have happened recently that I'm just a little stressed about.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me what's going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, yeah, so, uh, this week at work, um, there's, it's been happening for a little while, and I just confirmed that, and believe me, I'm the only person who hears this, um, I hear like this voice yelling at me. Um, and it's really freaking me out, because it, it happens and I, I can't explain how or why it's happening.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about what the voice is saying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, sometimes it's yelling at me to shut up, sometimes it whispers at me like "you suck". Um, but it's all these disparaging things that I'm just like, I, I just don't understand.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You recognize the voice?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not at all. Not at all.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's not similar to anybody that you've known or spoken to?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not that I can think of. Not, um, yeah, it doesn't sound like my mom or my dad or any of my friends, so it's just a random voice.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can other people hear it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, evidently not. Um, that's part of the reason why I came is because I was talking to one of my coworkers, um, and we were talking about something that we had to do at work, and um, in the middle of our conversation, I heard somebody say "shut up", and like, I turned and looked into the, my right, and my coworker's just like "what's going on?". I said like, "did you just hear that?". And I was just like, and my coworker was like "no, I didn't", and I was just like, "somebody just told me to shut up". And they were just like "no, I don't think, you're hearing things".

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: They didn't hear that.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They didn't hear it at all.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It was clear to you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It was really clear to me. Um, and then also sometimes when I'm sitting down just doing work at my desk, um, and I'm listening to music, sometimes I can hear the whisper or the shout then too. And I take off my headphones and nobody's in my cubicle area, nobody's talking to me, but I still hear it then too. And I know it's not in the song because I've been listening to this, this one artist for like the past three years and I love this CD and it, I know it's not in the CD.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so it's, it's something that you can hear and doesn't appear other people can hear it at all.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not at all.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you're sure there's no other explanation for it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: From what I know of, no, there's, I can't explain it. I can't explain it at all.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so you have those voices. Do you have anything that you're seeing that other people can't see?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, sometimes I feel as though that there's something like over my shoulder, and when I look there's nothing there. Um, but then also sometimes at work, like my cubicle's next to the hallway, sometimes I see like a shadow pop their head in and then go out. Um, and it happens randomly, and I'm just like, "did you just see that?". And most of my coworkers are like, "I don't know what you're talking about."

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do the, do the appearance of the shadows, does it seem to correspond in any way with the voices?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Generally, the voices will happen. Um, and then like an hour or two later, then like that shadowy figure happens. Um, and it could be just over my shoulder, it could be in the hallway, um, it could just be something down at the bottom of my desk, like it sometimes, it, they, I know when the voices happen, the shadow's going to come as well. And I just, and I stress myself out because I'm just like "crap, I just heard something, holy crap, something else is about to happen, I know it's going to happen, when is it going to happen?" and, and I just lose all concentration at work.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so this must be pretty stressful for you, right?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's, it's really stressful when it happens, but it doesn't happen all the time. That's the problem. Like, if it happened every day I could be like "okay, there's something really, really wrong". Um, but it happens like maybe once a week, maybe every other week. Um, this week it's been happening more for some odd reason, but it doesn't happen all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you remember when it first started, when that was?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I, I think it started like about three or four months ago. Um, yeah, it's about three or four months ago.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And it had never happened before?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It never happened before prior to that, never.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about your mood from that point until now?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've been a little bit more hypervigilant because I'm just like "why is this happening?" or like "I'm hearing this, is everybody else hearing it?". But otherwise, I'm, I'm myself. Most of my family and my friends, they're just like "dude, you're perfectly fine" and they haven't seen any change in my behavior.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Not more happy than usual, not more sad than usual, not more anxiety than usual?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, only time that stuff starts to change is when I have stuff to do at work, but I haven't had anything really major to do at work in the past three months, so not that stressful, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you think of anything else that might be causing it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, no, I, not that I'm aware of. I can't put my finger on anything that would actually cause this.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, I'm going to ask you a few questions, maybe find a connection. Any medical disorders, anything going on medically?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, not in my immediate family, not that I know of, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Have you ever been hospitalized?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I haven't even had a broken bone, so no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any use of drugs or alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I can't do any of that, I'm randomly drug tested at work and I just don't like the taste of alcohol.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any unusual stressors that have come up in the last, like since the symptoms appeared?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, well about four and a half-ish months ago, something, I, something happened on my way home from work one day.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, so, uh, I had to stay late at work to just to finish this project because it was due the next day. Um, and unfortunately, the bus stopped running then and um, I also, my ride wasn't there, so I had to walk home.
