diarization.text: Have you since the accident, or since the symptoms started, have you had positive feelings like happiness, joy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, everything just depresses me anymore. Everything. Nothing seems to be going right at all.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No? Not since the symptoms started.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you know how when something surprises you and you're startled? Right, that's natural for everybody. Have you noticed that that startle response is different now after the accident?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It is. Everything startles me. Just, you know, a knock at the door or the phone ringing or anything, just kind of scares me out of my skin.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So that's more so than it would have been in the past?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I've never been like that before.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any changes in your concentration?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I can't seem to focus on anything. Um, I'm in school and when I have readings to do for school, I just get so distracted, I have to close the book and do something else. I definitely can't focus when it comes to my schoolwork.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So when you're having trouble concentrating, what kind of thoughts are you being distracted toward?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: If I have somewhere to go, I'm thinking about getting in the car and driving and the possibility of being in another accident. I just a lot of my thoughts seem to focus on being in my car and just the accident. I can't seem to shake that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you've tried to push the thoughts aside and they're still there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any trouble sleeping?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Somewhat. Um, I don't have any trouble getting to sleep, but I have trouble staying to sleep.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you wake up several times at night?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about your relationship with other people? Do you feel there's the same distance, or do you feel closer or more detached?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, my mom is probably the person I'm closest to and I haven't really wanted to spend a lot of time with her anymore. I'm really just staying in the house and just staying to myself.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. How about dreams? Any change in dreams, like the events of the accident come up?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, one night there was this dream that stuck out to me. I was driving home from work and I was just about to get on the highway and I heard sirens coming. And I stopped to see where the sirens were going, and they got closer and closer to me, and they seemed to surround me. And I was like, wait, what's going on? And I woke up and I was like, oh my gosh, what? I felt like I was right back there in that moment where I was in a car accident and the police responded to the accident, but it was so much more intensified. I've never had a dream like that before.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And when you woke up, it sounds like you were alarmed and distressed. Is that ever happened when you weren't asleep, instead of like a dream? Have you ever had a moment where you're kind of back in the car accident as the accident's happening, like it feels like you're really back there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Maybe once or twice, but not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Not sure? No. All right. Do you have any medical problems?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Nothing going on? Any use of drugs or alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you remember all the details of the accident or do you feel like there's pieces of that memory that are missing?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I really can't remember the details. Um, I just know I got hit. I don't know back to what happened, and people keep asking me and I just can't remember at all really what happened.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So there's some memory loss surrounding that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, definitely.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever have, or since these symptoms have come on, do you ever feel like you're not really yourself? You're separated from yourself, kind of an unreal experience, or you're separated from the world, either one of those?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, Jessica, based on our conversation here, I'm going to set you up to see a counselor, if that's something you're open to. I want to thank you for taking the time to tell me what happened and answer my questions. It's been very helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #22 - Symptoms of Intermittent Explosive Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of intermittent explosive disorder (IED).

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi, Tiffany. How are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Hi. No, alright.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're alright?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Alright.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I understand you've been having some difficulty lately.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I wouldn't call it difficulty.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No? What would you call it?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, according to my husband, I'm having a little bit of trouble with anger or something like that, but to me it's like [pfft].

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so, so your husband believes you're having some trouble with anger?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: My husband thinks so, but to me I'm just fine. He's just... I may yell a little here and there at him, but he's a man. He should get over it. He's bigger than me, stronger than me. I've got, look, it's the way I get my point across. It's what I gotta do sometimes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I see. So you have a, you feel like you have a relational style that doesn't match with what he, he wants? Like you're, you're yelling and he's not liking that.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's how I communicate.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's how you communicate.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: If he's not happy with it, that's what, he's going to have to deal with it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about the, the yelling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: He says it's all the time. But to me, it's what I do. If I want him to take the trash out, I tell him to take the trash out. He says I yell at him. We get into a fight over it. It's just an argument over it, nothing serious. But he says it's for everything I do. Getting the kids ready to school, for school, he says I yell at the kids. He says, I can't make anything simple, I can't just make a simple request. He says I have to yell at him, I have to start a fight. I say he should man up.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you, you don't feel like you have a problem with yelling or anger or anything.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't think it's a problem, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's just the way you...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's the way I am.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's been causing you some, some trouble with your husband. Any other trouble?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, mainly with the husband. You know, I almost got into an argument with the neighbor, but we dealt with that. She told my husband, he agreed with her and well, he said I should get help.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so it's caused you, uh, some difficulties in that way.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: To me, it's not a difficulty. For him, it's more of a difficulty for him than it is for me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're really here today because he's asked you to come in?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm here. He's my husband. So I respect him. I want to make him happy. So I said I'll go.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, but you're, you're really not convinced that you...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't see it as a problem. Yeah. He's more of the problem than I am.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: He's convinced you're not.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I don't think I'm a problem. I don't think I have a problem. He says it's all the yelling and I need help and it's time I do something about it. I said, "Alright, fine. I'll go see about it."

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Would, uh, your relationship be a little easier without the yelling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: For him it would be, I guess. But it, it may be. We could try it, I don't know. But it's tough, it's what I do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about some of the events that, uh, you think lead to the yelling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: He doesn't get what I'm trying to say. It could be something as, he wants to do it his way. We could be driving. "Alright, no honey, I said we want to go this way." "Oh wait, why are you going that way?" "No, look." And then we get into a fight in the car. Or, "Okay honey, that's not how you do the dishes." Something as simple as that. "No, you wash, I dry." "No, that's not how you do the dishes." It could be something like that. We get into an argument. It's just over the simplest things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And in that argument, uh, how do you find the distribution of, like, who's yelling? Is it mostly you yelling or are you both yelling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I feel like I have to yell to get my point across, but he's not 100% innocent in this either. It's not my fault. I wouldn't have to yell if he listened the first time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever find yourself, uh, planning to get into an argument, or is it more spontaneous?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It just kind of happens when...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: If he would listen, we wouldn't be fighting so much. Things are fine when he listens. But then it's just, I don't know what it is, the moment I try to tell him something, it just, it just gets to me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And that's what leads to the yelling.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: We just start yelling, just start fighting.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. So this has been causing you some distress, mostly with that relationship.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Our relationship could be better if he would listen more, but yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Do you have any medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever use drugs or alcohol?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not an alcoholic or a drug addict or anything. If you're trying to say that, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Nothing like that. Do you have any other, uh, mental health history I should know about, like depression or anxiety?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I am as healthy as a horse.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Do you want to see a counselor here to work on the anger/yelling?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: If it would make him happy. I told him I would see a counselor, so I will see a counselor.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. So if you're okay with it, I'll set you up with an appointment to see a counselor here, and they should be able to see you within a couple days and you can get started.

diarization.speaker: Patient

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Thanks, Tiffany.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Alright.

diarization.speaker: Therapist

diarization.text: Yeah, you feel like you're getting a lot accomplished at work and at home. What types of things have you been doing?

diarization.speaker: Patient

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: He's worried because I went on a shopping spree. He doesn't really know how much I am making with this new promotion. diarization.text: Alright, so you haven't gotten in any trouble at work or at home or anything?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not at all. Like I said, I got a promotion at work. My bosses are extremely happy with how productive I've been and the quality of my work. I'm able to look over the reports I turn in several times before I do it, and I always make sure I do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. Any changes with your sleep habits?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes and no. I mean, yes because I haven't really been sleeping as much as I used to. I think I used to sleep too much, but I haven't needed to this week. It hasn't been an issue; it's actually been a good thing.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So how much did you sleep last night?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Just about an hour and a half.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you feel rested.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I do feel rested. I might take a thirty-minute nap later, but then I'll be fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so you have a lot of energy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any feelings of depression or anything like that, sadness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I feel great.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever had anything like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I have, actually. In the past, I was diagnosed with depression, so I know what it feels like, and I know that I don't have anything like that right now.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How long ago was that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: A few years ago.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any thoughts about death or dying or anything related to that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not really. I mean, obviously you hear about people dying on TV or friends and family members, but I don't dwell on it. I feel like in the past I might have, but I haven't been.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any drug or alcohol use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How are you doing medically? Anything medically going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I'm healthy.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. And do you see or hear anything that things that other people can't see or hear?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has it ever happened?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright Sherry. You answering these questions for me has been helpful. I know that you're feeling well, but I'd like you to talk to a counselor if that's okay. I know that you're aware your brother's concerned.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: That's why I'm here for him.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're here for him? Okay. So if it'd be okay with you, I'd like you to speak with a counselor at least for a little bit, and I can arrange that in just a few moments if that's okay.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: That's fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thanks.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mhm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so you're feeling you're feeling pretty good?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mhm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you have been for about a week?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.text: All right. Have you do you feel like um your sleep habits have changed?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right so you're sleeping less but you don't feel tired at all?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mmm-mmm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No, nothing like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mmm-mmm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You mentioned you're getting a lot of things done at work. How about at home?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. I mean, um so my dining room, I've needed like more new china and stuff like that, so I've gotten everything set up. diarization.text: All right, so you're accomplishing you're accomplishing a lot. Now when your brother had brought you in, he had mentioned some shopping, and that's one of the things he was concerned about.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, well, so um on the weekend I had gone ahead and went shopping and I kind of went on a shopping spree, um and I had bought like I said my new china, and I'd gotten some kitchen utensils too and a couple things for around the house like home decor. Um and he has an SUV, so I called him to see if he could come um and so I could purchase the the items, but he said he wasn't he couldn't come out and he I guess he kind of said he was worried about me spending that much money, um which I don't you know, I don't know why he would be just from me calling him, but I think that's why he was concerned. diarization.text: Do you feel like you spent more than you usually would spend at a trip to the mall?

diarization.text: All right. Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt this way, where you felt really good?

diarization.text: Life's fallen into place. So you're feeling pretty good, you feel like things are going your way?

diarization.text: I do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you're getting a lot accomplished.

diarization.text: Mhm.

diarization.text: Any sadness or anything like that?

diarization.text: No.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #21 - Client with Symptoms of Bipolar Disorder

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Sherry, how are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Great, how are you?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm doing well, thanks for asking.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: That's awesome.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're doing great?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I am doing awesome.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I know your brother brought you in today and he had expressed some concerns about your mood. Do you know what that's about?

diarization.text: All right, so you feel like everything's kind of going your way and you're really excited about the new business idea. diarization.text: All right, he's worried that you don't know the guy too well.

diarization.speaker: Patient

diarization.text: All right, so your brother just doesn't get it.

diarization.text: All right. Have you noticed through all this any change in sleep patterns?

diarization.text: All right, so you do feel rested but you haven't been sleeping as much.

diarization.text: No.

diarization.text: And you clearly seem like you're in a good mood. No sadness or anything like that?

diarization.text: And realizing that's changed your life?

diarization.text: All right, so you're not too worried about that. Any medical conditions you know of?

diarization.text: How about drug and alcohol use? Any of that?

diarization.text: Sherry, I know that you're feeling pretty well, but I would like you to see a counselor to help you as you contemplate these things. Would you be okay with that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess I'd be fine.

diarization.text: You'd be okay with that?

diarization.text: Mhmm.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #17 - Client with Symptoms of Depression
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sherry, how are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm doing okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're doing okay? I understand you haven't been feeling too great lately.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, yeah. I'm never like feeling awesome really, but lately it's come to my awareness that something might be wrong.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Something might be wrong? In what way?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, it's not anything new, but I have a lot of trouble sleeping. I wake up always really early and then I can't get back to sleep.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. So you're waking up earlier than you want to?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, and I can't get back to sleep no matter how hard I try. I don't have a lot of energy, but it's hard for me to get to sleep. It's been like that since high school.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Lately I realized some days are better than others, but something happened a couple weeks ago that made me feel like I should talk to someone.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What happened?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: My brother got married and I was really looking forward to it, but I just didn't have as much fun as I thought I would. It's just my mood, I'm always a little gloomy.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So your mood didn't elevate like maybe you hoped it would.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it just wasn't as fun as I wanted it to be or as I thought it would be.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And realizing this is what brought you in today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, and right afterwards I had more worse days than better days. I just didn't feel excited like everyone else. I was just more down.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I was happier than I would be if I was staying home by myself, but I wasn't like everyone else.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so you mentioned that this has been going on from high school?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So how long would that be?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, I mean, I graduated in 2010, so eight years.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So about eight years and you've been feeling down. Has the sleep been a problem for that long?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, a little bit when I was in high school. My sleep schedule never came to that normal eight hours a night.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah, you mentioned the word gloomy.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And the low energy has been a problem for that long as well?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you've been waking up earlier than you want to?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You mentioned the depressed mood. You feel down. Is that worse at any particular time of the day?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it's worse in the morning. Especially when I'm just sitting there with my thoughts when I can't get back to sleep.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: As the day goes on I forget about it a little bit and it gets a little bit better in the afternoons and nighttime.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: In the morning, the morning's the worst.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so I'm going to ask you some other questions. Have you lost interest in other things that might be fun or pleasurable?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I haven't really lost an interest in anything. I still seek out fun activities but my response to them isn't as high as other people.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You enjoy it, just not as much. Any changes to your appetite or weight?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, stays the same.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. How about feelings of restlessness or being slowed down?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Ever feel a sense of worthlessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about concentration, how's that been?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: It's fine. I can focus on what I need to focus on.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You do okay with that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever have thoughts of death or dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. Any drug or alcohol use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: About medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever seen or heard things other people cannot see or hear?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever had a time when your mood was too happy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not really. There's been times on vacation where I've noticed I was happier but nothing ever more than a couple days.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. You ever been hospitalized before?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have feelings of hopelessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And how's your self-esteem?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright Sherry, I'd like to get you in to see a counselor here. It'll probably take a couple days to get you in with somebody. Is that okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that's okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I appreciate you answering these questions for me. This has been helpful.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #15 - Client with Symptoms of Depression
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sherry, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've been better.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You've been better? I understand you haven't been feeling so well lately.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I haven't.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I think I've been depressed for about two months and it's been getting worse and that's why I'm here. Um, you know, I haven't been sleeping very well. I haven't had much of an appetite, haven't been eating very well, and you know, the last couple months I've lost a bit of weight from it. Okay. You know, I'm tired all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Tired all the time?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mm-hmm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find that you have low energy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you say this has been going on for a couple months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, for about two months.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Did anything major happen that you think might have brought this on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, I mean, a big thing that happened between five and six months ago is my cat died. Um, and you know, I was sad for a little bit and I'll have days where I miss him, but the last two months have been nothing like what I felt when he died.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: The last two months the symptoms have been more severe or less severe?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: More severe.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So your cat passed away six months ago.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And these symptoms you've had for the last two months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're not sure if they're really related?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I don't know. Like I do miss my cat, but...

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you think about your cat most days or how often?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, just... I would say, you know, a couple times a week it will hit me that he's gone, he's not there. Um, and I'll think about him, but you know, I'll have bad days without thinking about missing him. And so I don't know if it's that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I'm gonna ask you some other questions related to depression, if that's okay.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you noticed any change in your interest in seeking fun or pleasure, like in how you approach pleasurable activities?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, I feel like I'm still trying to have fun, you know, like I know what I like to do and I'll try to do those things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What types of things do you still try to do?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Like I like going out to dinner with my sister and I kind of like reading books and watching movies, so I'll try to do that and enjoy it. Sometimes it's hard for me to concentrate when I'm reading or watching a movie, like I'll get distracted, but I still try.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You still try?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mm-hmm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Ever feel restless or kind of the opposite of that, like slowed down, like you can't move as fast as...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean, I have noticed that as you know, the last couple months, like at work, it will be hard for me, like it just feels like time's going so slowly and I just, almost like I'm in a dream and like I can't move. It's weird.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you feel slowed down?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any feelings of worthlessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Can you tell me about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: You know, I just don't think that anyone really cares about what happens to me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about your ability to concentrate? Any changes there over the last two months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, like it's harder for me to like pay attention to movies and stuff, and at work, I don't know if it's because I'm tired or what, but it's hard for me to pay attention to the projects I'm supposed to be working on, and I have noticed, yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any thoughts related to death or dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No? Any drug or alcohol use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: None.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: None. Do you ever see or hear things other people can't see or hear?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not recently, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about before that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, well years ago I was hospitalized, but it was because my neighbors said that I was hearing things and saying things that I didn't say, like about the government, but I haven't had anything like that happen for years.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So this is years ago you were hospitalized? Did they tell you anything about that hospitalization, like exactly why?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I don't remember.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you feel depressed back then like you do now?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, maybe. I think probably some of the same things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: But it sounds like it's not clear in your memory what happened.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever had a period of time where you're too happy, where you had like a lot of energy and just couldn't stop moving?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Nothing like that, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right Sherry, I'm going to get you in to see a counselor. It'll just take a couple days for us to get you in to see somebody and it's my hope that they can help you. I want to thank you for answering these questions, this has been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #18 - Client with Symptoms of Bipolar Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of bipolar disorder.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sherry, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Doing okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're doing okay? I understand you haven't been feeling too well lately, like you've had some symptoms. Tell me what's going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, so for almost a week now, every little thing irritates me. It's distracting how much little things are bothering me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Little things are really irritating you for the last week?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is this the first time this has happened?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So tell me about the irritation. Like what kind of things have been...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: At work, the guy in the cubicle next to me clears his throat or blows his nose every 15 minutes. It drives me crazy. I can't focus, so I try to put on music, then my boss gets upset because I have earbuds in. When I'm driving home, there was a guy walking his dog on the side of the road with no shoulder, and I felt like he was risking everyone's lives. Everything people do is driving me up the wall.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so you're really irritated and you feel like these events are distracting you.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you feel like your thoughts are racing?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'll be trying to focus and all these things are irritating me. My thoughts will race through different things and it makes me more frustrated and anxious.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You mentioned work. Have you found that you're more oriented toward getting goals completed?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, no, not anymore so than usual.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find yourself talking more or feeling like you should talk more?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I actually don't want to talk to people because I feel like something they say will annoy me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How's your sleep been?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Fine. Sometimes it takes a while for my thoughts to shut down when I'm first going to bed, but it doesn't take too long.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so your sleep's been okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you noticed that you're at all down or have a depressed mood?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Are you still finding activities that were pleasurable to be pleasurable now?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. Sometimes I get distracted by something that irritates me, but for the most part I can enjoy things I genuinely like.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any change in your appetite?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about any feelings of worthlessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You mentioned being distracted easily. Is that affecting your concentration?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: A little bit.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you have any thoughts regarding death or dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: This irritable mood has been bothering you at work and driving home. Any other places?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, something my mom said on the phone irritated me, and I cut the call short and didn't talk to my dad because I was mad. It's affecting my personal life too.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any drug or alcohol usage recently?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever seen or heard things other people can't see or hear?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, that's never happened.

diarization.speaker: Ther therapist
diarization.text: Okay. I'd like to get you in to see a counselor today if that's okay. They can talk to you more about this. Would that be all right?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mhmm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. I'll get that arranged and I want to thank you for answering these questions, this has been helpful.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #14 - Client with Symptoms of Depression
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi, Sherry. How are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm doing okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're doing okay? I understand you've been having some symptoms which have been bothering you a bit. Can you tell me what you think's going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, um, I've been feeling really low and I think I might be depressed.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You think you might be depressed? Have you ever felt this way in the past?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, years ago, I you know, felt had some of these similar things, but I didn't really think about it much. And I mean this has been going on for like, I've been feeling this way for like a month and, you know, I think something's wrong.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You've been having feelings of sadness, hopelessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah. I mean, you know, I haven't been able to sleep.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Trouble sleeping? And this has been going on for a month?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you noticed any change in your ability to experience fun or pleasure?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I haven't really thought about it, but I mean I still have fun sometimes, but I've noticed that most of the time I'm sad.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Most of the time you're sad, but you still have fun? Have you lost an interest in pursuing things that are fun?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I mean I still try, you know, to distract myself, like if I notice that I'm like just feeling really low and or like even if I can't sleep at night, like I'll do go do something that I like doing you know, to pass the time. Like I watch movies and stuff.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any change in your appetite or weight in the last couple weeks?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean I haven't really been eating that much and I've actually lost a few pounds.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Lost a few pounds? And you mentioned the sleep disturbance, how you've not been sleeping as much as you'd like to.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Correct. It's really hard for me to fall asleep and sometimes I'll just lie there for hours at night and it's you know, awful because then I'm tired all day because I didn't sleep at night. And when I get home and it's time for bed again, I still can't fall asleep.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so that's been affecting your energy level?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you feel restless or the opposite, kind of like slowed down? You been having either one of those feelings?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, no, not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you been having any feelings of worthlessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I mean you know, like not really, no. Like I don't feel worthless. I just you know, I just I'm still sad though I don't know why I'm sad.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about um your concentration level? Any changes there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, it's it's hard to concentrate at work and and in general, even at home because I just because I'm so tired, I'm not sleeping and sometimes I just get distracted by like you know, like I'll be overcome with emotion and out of nowhere and like it's hard for me to pay attention to what I'm doing if I'm getting distracted by those thoughts.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you been having any thoughts related to death or dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So these symptoms you've been describing have been causing limitations in your functioning in what areas?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: At work. At work, um at home too, you know like I want to play with my cat. I usually play with my cat for like an hour every night just because you know I'm at work all day. But I haven't, I've been having trouble like even doing that and um yeah. So I would say and then even like my relationships too, like my social life, it's been affecting it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Any drug or alcohol use? How about any medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever see or hear things other people can't see or hear? Has it ever happened to you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. Never.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you feel now, recently or ever, you ever had a state where you were too happy? Like have a lot of energy and...

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Like mania? No. Nothing like that ever.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has there been any major event in the last month or maybe before that that you think might be causing this?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. Nothing significant happened to make me feel this way.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Nothing you think would cause depression?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright Sherry. I'm going to get you in to see a counselor here, but it'll take a couple days to get you in, is that okay? I want to thank you for answering these questions for me. This has been helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes. You're welcome.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #13 - Client with Symptoms of Depression
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi, Sherry. How you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. I understand you've been having some symptoms which have been bothersome. Can you tell me about those?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Main thing is I'm just sleeping all the time. I'm really tired. I'm tired when I have to go to work, and then I go home and I just sleep a lot and I think it's abnormal. I haven't been eating as much lately, I've lost a bit of weight. And it's just affecting my life, so I just wanted to come in.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright, so you have excessive sleep? What is excessive sleep?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Like just hours. I'll get home from work and take a three hour nap and then I'll wake up and do something I enjoy, but then it'll be bedtime again and I'll be ready for bed even though I took a nap. I'll sleep in every chance I get.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And you mentioned your appetite as well.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I don't know if it's because I'm sleeping so much I'm not eating, but when I wake up it's not like I'm hungry. Nothing.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How long have these symptoms been present?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've noticed it in the last two weeks or so. I've noticed that it's been getting worse.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Over the last two weeks? Out of one week, how many days do you have these symptoms?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Probably every day.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. In the last two weeks, have you found yourself depressed, sad, hopeless, anything like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you lost interest in activities that used to be fun for you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I still like all the things I did, like all my hobbies and hanging out with friends. Sometimes it's hard for me to remember to make plans and I just end up sleeping instead, but I genuinely enjoy it still.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever feel agitated in terms of movement? Like you can't stop moving or find yourself trying to resist movement?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess not so much I can't stop moving, but I do try to stop myself from fidgeting sometimes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any changes in terms of your level of energy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I'm tired all the time. I've been late to work just because I haven't had the energy to get up and stop sleeping.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so the excessive sleep has affected your energy. How about any type of feeling of worthlessness?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I guess yeah. It sounds harsh, but I'm not really a valuable person. I don't have an important job, no one really depends on me.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You don't view yourself as valuable?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, not really. But it is what it is.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And how long have you felt this way?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: For a while. You know when you don't contribute very much. So it is what it is.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about your concentration? Have you found any changes there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: At work, yes, definitely. I'll be tired and yawning. Even outside of work, I'll forget to make plans or forget little things. It's hard for me to pay attention to movies.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're having trouble focusing?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever have any thoughts of death or dying?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. Nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You mentioned problems at work. Any other areas where they've been causing you trouble?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: You mean like with social life?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Social life, relationships, life at home?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I live on my own and sleeping all the time means I don't see anyone else. It's hard to meet new people. I'll sleep instead of making plans with friends on a Friday night, so that can't be good.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about substances? Do you use any alcohol or drugs?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I'll drink socially but I haven't really done that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, none.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever see or hear things other people can't see or hear?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever had a period in your life or now where you're extremely happy and have a lot of energy?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, nothing like that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright Sherry, I'm going to refer you to see a counselor. I could schedule you in to see them in the next couple days?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, that works fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I appreciate you answering these questions, this has been helpful. Thank you.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Thanks.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #16 - Client with Symptoms of Depression
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits symptoms of depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sherry, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm doing okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're doing okay? I understand your father brought you in today. He's a little worried about how you might be feeling.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, yeah. I mean, he's worried that I'm depressed, but I'm not.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah, he had mentioned that you had some concerns about some things going on in your neighborhood and that you called the police a few times.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: He told you that? Well, yeah. I mean, I have called the police a few times because there's something going on in my neighborhood. And it makes me seem like I'm depressed, but I'm not. I'm just concerned about what's going on.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you're not depressed, you're more concerned. So what's going on where you live that's leading to these feelings?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, well, it's actually very scary. I know about the government kidnapping girls in this area and taking them away for sex trafficking and prostitution.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Right. So you believe the government is apprehending people in the area where you live.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I know they are.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You know they are. And did you see anything specifically that led you to believe this?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, yes. There specifically were two girls that lived down the street and I saw a van come down the street and the girls were taken. That's when I initially called the police, but I found out they're in on it too.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: The police are in on it too?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes. They tried to tell me that the girls are safe and with their aunt, but I know they're not.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So they investigated what you saw and they came back and told you—

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They pretended to.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: They pretended to investigate. And they came back and told you everything was okay, but you're not—

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, I know it's a lie because I haven't seen the girls since. Like, I saw the girls on the street, the van came, the girls weren't there. They told me everything's fine, but I know that's a lie and I won't go back to the police again because I know that they're now in on it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: They're in on what the government's been doing. So, what do you think of your father's concerns? You know, he's concerned that you're down or depressed and that your thinking hasn't been clear. What do you think about his concerns?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I mean, I know he's worried about me, but he just doesn't understand the severity of the situation. And it's hard to sleep when I'm thinking about these poor girls. And the government has cameras everywhere. They can watch what I'm doing at all times and it's exhausting.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: So I can see how he would think I'm depressed because I'm not sleeping well, and I'm not eating 'cause what if they poisoned my food? They're poisoning water all the time. So, you know, it is scary and it is affecting me, but it's not depression.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're not depressed.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. I'm sad for those girls and I'm scared for me and what's going on, but I want to make sure that this doesn't happen again because I can't let this continue. So that's what's taking up my time right now.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And how long has this been going on?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: For a few months.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: For a few months. Is that when you first saw what you believe to be the kidnapping?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: When I saw the kidnapping, yes. That was a few months ago.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Were there any beliefs like this before two months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, yes. I've always been aware that the government is probably up to things that they probably shouldn't be. But after I saw the kidnapping, I had proof, and so it's gotten worse because I feel like they know that I know.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So you've felt this way for a while, but seeing what you saw two months ago, that made you more sure.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, because now I have proof.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever been treated for depression in the past?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, yes. My dad has taken me before when he was worried about me. But it's never really been depression. It's always been something else. I'm fine, I'm just aware of what's going on around me and I don't think my dad understands that and I don't think the places he takes me understand that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: What have the people at the places where he has taken you said about your condition?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: They try to say the same thing, that I'm depressed or whatever, but I know the truth and sometimes I just have to play along.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You just play along with it.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, because this is what the government wants. They want me to look crazy. There's nothing I can do about it.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you think they want to discredit you.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, because it's kind of like smearing my good name. They see me in and out of different agencies and appearing crazy. Obviously, a lot of people don't believe the story. They choose not to believe or they get paid off and they write what they write on my file, but it's not true. I just know what's going on.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And because you know what's going on, that's what's led to all these occurrences. This has led to the symptoms.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, like lately. I haven't been able to sleep, and I feel guilty about what's going on and that it's hard for me to help them with cameras everywhere. I can't even go to the grocery store without being watched. I do everything I'm supposed to. I go to work and do the chores because I have to make sure they see me doing those things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you kind of play along.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So do you ever have any thoughts related to death or dying or anything like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're worried about what?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm worried about the government destroying my life. But I don't want to die and I don't think they're going to kill me. I think that would be too easy and it would just be more proof.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: That'd be more proof that what you've seen is real.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Correct. Because obviously I'm trying to tell people about it, and if I suddenly show up missing, people are going to know. So I know that they're not going to hurt me, but they could make me look crazy. I'm worried about them ruining my life.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Ruining it that way.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Mm-hm.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. How about any drug or alcohol abuse or anything like that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No. I don't like to use those things.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Any medical conditions?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Has there ever been a time when you felt really very happy, like a lot of energy and was very happy for several days?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not really.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: That's never happened.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you ever heard or seen things other people can't hear or see?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I think that I'm aware of things that people aren't, no.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Have you been hospitalized before?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes. But again, it was—I had tried to initially tell my dad about some things that I knew about and he had taken me to the hospital, but that was before.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. So I would like to get you in to talk to a counselor today. How do you feel about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Is it really necessary today? Like, can I come back another day?

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I think it would be helpful if we had a counselor talk to you today.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, I understand that's what you need to do. So if that's what we need to do to get this over with, that's fine.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You can be okay with that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: M-hm. I can play along.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You can play along. All right, Sherry, I want to thank you for answering these questions. I know this is a tough experience for you. It's been helpful for you to answer these questions for me. I'll just need a couple minutes and I'll get you over to see a counselor and we'll kind of go from there.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thanks, Sherry.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: You're welcome.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #12 - Client with Features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sarah, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, hi. Um, I'm doing all right today.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're doing all right today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I am doing all right today, yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I understand that you've been having some symptoms and that's what has brought you into our agency. Could you tell me about that?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I've been having a lot of worry.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: A lot of worry?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, a lot of worry on and off for, um, about the past four or five months maybe. Maybe about six months, just around four, five, six months. And I just started back to school after being a stay-at-home mom for 20 years. The kids are all off to college now in a way and I decided why not go back to school, do something else now. And it's just been causing and well, I've just been worried so much lately.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so, so a lot of worry. Somewhere at four or five or six months it's been going on. Have you had this worry more days than you haven't had it in that last four to six months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I've had a lot of good days. I mean, I've had some bad days but I've had a lot of good days too. So, um, I don't know.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay, not quite sure.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Not quite sure.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find the worry difficult to control?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, when I do worry, yes. Yes, very much so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. So I'm going to ask you some questions related to this, all right? Let me know if you've experienced these symptoms. Do you feel restless, keyed up, or on edge?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, yes I do.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. How about, are you easily tired?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: All the time. So tired all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah, all the time?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you ever have trouble concentrating or finding your mind go blank?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I find my mind just wandering, just going blank. I would call that going blank, yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. Do you find that you've been irritable?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Very much so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any muscle tension?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, just rigidness.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: And tell me about how you've been sleeping.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, not very well. I would say not very well lately. Finding it hard, just I can't go to sleep and I can't stay asleep. It's just been hard.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Do you drink alcohol or use any drugs?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, I don't.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Have you ever had a panic attack?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Any trauma in your history?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Any mental health disorders at all?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Do you find the symptoms very distressing?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, yes, distressing.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yes. And what areas are they distressing?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, at home, so much at home. Yeah, like I'm doing great in school.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: School's okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: School's, um, 4.0.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Wow, very good.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes. Um, just at home, I'm just in a constant state of worry all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about when you go out with friends?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Have fun! Great times, great times with my friends, yes. I love going out.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Is there something specific to your home environment you think might be contributing to this, because you don't have it at school, you don't have it socially?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah, I mean, we have some problems here and there.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Some problems here and there?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh-huh.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Nothing you could isolate as maybe causing these symptoms?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, one does maybe, maybe not things, but just nothing I can't work through.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Nothing you can't work through?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, Sarah. So I'm going to get you in to see one of our counselors, if that's okay with you. It'll just take a couple days for you to get an appointment set and for you to get in. Is that okay? To see a counselor in a couple days?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I would like that very much, yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay, I'll get that set up, and I want to thank you for answering these questions. It's been really helpful to me.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, thank you.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #11 - Client with Features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sarah, how you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Uh, I'm okay. Could be better, could be worse. Um, I'm hanging in there.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: You're hanging in there? I understand you've been having some symptoms that have been bothering you. Can you tell me about those?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, I'm worried all the time and just every day, all day, just so worried about everything. I've just started back to school after 20 years. I've been a housewife, the kids are now grown. So why not go back to school? And now for the past seven or eight months, it's just been nothing but worry, worry, worry, constantly all the time. Worried about home, worried about school, and it's affecting my life.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Right, so a lot of- a lot of worrying. And how many days would you say you worry in a typical week?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: How many days don't I worry? Um, I'd say most days. Monday through Friday, I'm worried about school, or when I'm at school, I'm worried about home, and then on the weekends, I know the school week's coming up and then I just worry about managing everything. So I'd say it's a lot.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Right, so it's very distressing for you. And you mentioned it's impacting school?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, school, I'm not doing too well right now. When I was in undergrad, I used to be a straight-A student, but right now, I'm worried so much that my grades are slipping. When I'm in school, I'm still worried about what's going on at home that I can't pay attention in class, and it's just all-consuming.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Mm. All right, so both at school and at home. You find it difficult to control the anxiety? And it's affecting you in a major way.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yes, very much so.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: I might ask you some other questions that may be tied in with this, okay? Do you use any alcohol or drugs?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Some. I have a drink occasionally, but my nerves are always on edge right now that I find it helps. So, I mean, I've got it under control.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: It's under control? How often would you say you drink?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, maybe some here and there every day.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Yeah. And how much would you say you drink?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Maybe a few glasses of wine a night. But I'm not an alcoholic or anything.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. How about the drug use?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: A little pot now and then, like maybe a couple times a week. I find it helps my nerves.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. Have you ever had a panic attack?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: No. Have you ever had any trauma in your history?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, my grandma, she died when I was young. She used to take care of us. She was like a second mom to me, and I was really close to her. I think about her a lot now, especially since I started back to school. She always encouraged me to get an education, and now I've just been thinking about her a lot.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so she's been on your mind. And when you think about her, what's the feeling that comes up?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I worry a lot because I think I'm upsetting her and her memory if I don't do well. Even though I know she's not here anymore, she'd be upset if I'm not doing well.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, so when you're thinking about her, you're having some worry. That's been distressing you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Very much, yes.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right, I'm going to ask you about some symptoms. Let me know if you've had these. Do you feel restless, keyed up, or on edge?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: All the time. Just so tense.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: All right. How about- do you feel like you get tired easily?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm tired all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: How about- do you find your mind going blank or having trouble concentrating?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Well, I find I'm trying to think of so many things at once that I can't focus just on one thing, so yes, definitely having trouble concentrating.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Have you noticed that you're more irritable?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: I'm not sleeping a lot, so I'm cranky. According to my husband, a lot irritable.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Now you mentioned you're tense all the time, is that like a muscle tension?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Pretty much. Just feel like my muscles are going to snap. I feel so rigid all the time.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Okay. And tell me about your sleep.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Sleep's been non-existent pretty much right now. Trying to go to sleep when you have so much on your mind is hard.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So you have difficulty falling asleep? How about once you fall asleep, do you stay asleep?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: No, because I'll have nightmares that will just wake me up, and then I find myself wondering what I'm forgetting. It's just some ugly cycle going on right now.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: So the sleep has been a big problem for you. Sarah, I'd like to get you in to see a counselor. I can probably get you in to see one in just a couple days, if that's okay?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, I would appreciate that.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Would that be helpful? And I want to thank you for answering these questions for me. This has been really helpful.

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Oh, thank you very much.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Thanks, Sarah.

video_details.title: Counseling Diagnostic Assessment Vignette #10 - Client with Features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder
video_details.description: This counseling diagnostic assessment vignette demonstrates an interview with a client (played by an actress) who exhibits features of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Hi Sarah, how are you doing today?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I'm doing okay. Could be a little bit better, but I could always be worse, but I'm doing okay.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Doing okay? I understand you have some symptoms that have been bothering you?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, they have been bothering me. Well, I just started back to school last year. I was staying at home while my husband was working, but the kids are grown now, out of the house, so I said I was going to go back to school. I haven't been in school in 20 years, and I thought I could handle it, but right now I just find myself so anxious and just so worried all the time, and I just don't know what to do with it. It's been going on for around the past seven, eight months now.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: About seven or eight months?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Yeah.

diarization.speaker: Therapist
diarization.text: Alright. Would you say that this anxiety has been affecting you more days than it doesn't?

diarization.speaker: Patient
diarization.text: Um, I would say it's been affecting me, yes, for some time now, yes. More often than not, yes.
